correctness.rationale: The same-column pair in each open neighborhood has one common graph neighbor; it certifies both elementary removals for all centers. For n=3 or n≥5, the parity-preserving deck lattice has no nonzero element of Manhattan length below six, making the survivor the genuine quotient of a triangular plane by a rank-two translation lattice. An odd horizontal period joins the two parity sheets. Thus the 3n-vertex core is a connected orientable PL torus, and its integral fundamental/homology/cohomology statements follow. For n=4 independent exact face counts (12,42,48,12) give Euler characteristic six. For n≥6 divisible by3, all graph triangles are columns, yielding automorphism group S3×Dn, which has no cyclic order-3n element. The standalone program independently checks all free-face conditions, counts, orientations and links for n=3,5..40; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A motivated, complete infinite classification of a canonical short-period branch of open-neighborhood topology, including a sharp exceptional cycle length. It closes the first short-systole gap of an existing square-torus classification, and proves a change from wedge-of-spheres topology at clique widths ≥4 to a true torus with nonzero degree-one cup product at width three. Noncirculant 3-divisible cases cannot be obtained from prior circulant computations, and 6n explicit free-face pairs give a reproducible simple-homotopy strengthening.
